machine: CPU (Mac, 16 GB, float64); no GPU — the eigensolves are sequential sparse shift-invert solves, not parallel-shaped, so the compute protocol's CPU default applies (no A100 case)
note: active = sum of per-candidate wall time (T2) + other step timers. It is NOT the step log alone: after the D4 restart each candidate ran in its own `--one` process that exits before main()'s timer fires, so the step log alone would report ~15 s for a ~7.7 h compute. Eigensolve time is measured inside enrich() and is a SUBSET of the candidate wall time (itemised here, not added twice).

thrash_incident.what: the single long-lived T2 process drove the 16 GB box to 10.8/12.3 GB swap by candidate ~18; one eigensolve took 11187 s vs a 506 s median (22x)
thrash_incident.fix: killed and restarted with ONE candidate per process (decisions_log D4)
thrash_incident.science_impact: none — a slow ARPACK solve is still an exact solve; the affected candidate (wr2_rnd001) reproduces the study's independently-computed exact score to 1e-5 and its self-consistency is 8.5e-8 %
thrash_incident.cost: wall-clock only; elapsed_wallclock_s is inflated by roughly 3 h of thrash

sampler_note: no sampler was run in this card (decisions_log D0)
